22385.q: Which vehicle does Doc Brown turn into a time machine in “Back to the Future”?
22385.e: Doc Brown turns a DeLorean sports car into a time machine. At 88 miles per hour, the car travels through time.
22385.m: In “Back to the Future” people travel through time in a converted car.

22386.q: What is the name of Dorothy’s little dog in the 1939 film “The Wizard of Oz”?
22386.e: Toto goes with Dorothy on her journey through the Land of Oz. The film is one of the best-known early colour films.
22386.m: Dorothy’s dog Toto is always with her in “The Wizard of Oz”.

22387.q: In the film “Jurassic Park”, where does the dinosaurs’ DNA come from?
22387.e: In the film, mosquitoes sucked dinosaur blood millions of years ago and were then trapped in tree resin. Scientists get the DNA from the blood.
22387.m: In “Jurassic Park” the dinosaur DNA comes from mosquitoes in amber.

22388.q: In “Star Wars”, who is Luke Skywalker’s father?
22388.e: In “The Empire Strikes Back” (1980), Darth Vader reveals that he is Luke’s father. He used to be called Anakin Skywalker.
22388.m: Darth Vader is Luke Skywalker’s father.

22389.q: What is the film character Indiana Jones’s job?
22389.e: Indiana Jones is a professor of archaeology and searches for famous treasures on adventurous journeys. He is played by Harrison Ford.
22389.m: Indiana Jones is an adventurous archaeologist.

22390.q: What is the name of the founder of the studio that brought out Mickey Mouse?
22390.e: Walt Disney founded a cartoon studio with his brother Roy in 1923. Mickey Mouse became the studio’s best-known character.
22390.m: Walt Disney founded one of the most famous film studios in the world.

22391.q: Which studio made the animated films “Ratatouille” and “Up”?
22391.e: Pixar Animation Studios from California specialises in computer-animated films. Since 2006 Pixar has belonged to Disney.
22391.m: Pixar is a studio for computer-animated films.

22392.q: In which country does the well-known animation studio Ghibli have its headquarters?
22392.e: Studio Ghibli was founded in Tokyo in 1985. Its hand-drawn films are loved all over the world.
22392.m: Studio Ghibli is an animation studio from Japan.

22393.q: In which country is Aardman, the studio that created “Shaun the Sheep”?
22393.e: Aardman Animations is based in Bristol in England. The studio is famous for its plasticine figures.
22393.m: Aardman is an English studio for plasticine films.

22394.q: Which animal roars at the start of films by the studio Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM)?
22394.e: The roaring lion has been MGM’s trademark for almost 100 years. Over time, several different lions have been filmed.
22394.m: At MGM a lion roars before every film.

22395.q: Why do film studios shoot many scenes in large halls instead of outdoors?
a: Because light, sound and weather can be controlled there
Because cameras do not work outside
Because halls are cheaper than cameras
22395.e: In a studio hall, neither rain nor traffic noise gets in the way. The team can set up the lighting and scenery exactly as the scene needs. A famous example is Babelsberg Studio near Berlin.
22395.m: In a studio, light, sound and weather can be controlled.

22396.q: Which company bought Lucasfilm, and with it the rights to “Star Wars”, in 2012?
22396.e: Disney took over Lucasfilm in 2012 for around 4 billion US dollars. After that, new “Star Wars” films and series were made.
22396.m: Since 2012, “Star Wars” has belonged to Disney.

22397.q: Which studio made the animated film “Shrek” in 2001?
22397.e: With “Shrek”, DreamWorks Animation put a cheeky ogre at the centre of the story. The film became a successful series.
22397.m: “Shrek” comes from the studio DreamWorks Animation.

22398.q: Which studio created the yellow Minions?
22398.e: The Minions first appeared in 2010 in the film “Despicable Me” by the studio Illumination. Later they got their own films.
22398.m: The Minions come from the studio Illumination.

22399.q: What is the big film industry in Mumbai (India) called?
22399.e: The name Bollywood is made from Bombay, the former name of Mumbai, and Hollywood. India makes a great many films every year.

22400.q: Which Disney film from 1937 was the studio’s first full-length animated film?
a: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
22400.e: “Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs” came out in cinemas in 1937. Many thought the project was too risky, but it was a huge success.
22400.m: In 1937, “Snow White” was Disney’s first full-length animated film.

22401.q: Which 1995 film was the first full-length cinema film to be animated entirely on a computer?
22401.e: In “Toy Story”, toys such as Woody and Buzz Lightyear come to life. All the pictures in the film were made on a computer.
22401.m: “Toy Story” is the first fully computer-animated cinema film.

22402.q: What is the animation technique called in which figures made of plasticine or wood are moved slightly and photographed picture by picture?
22402.e: In stop motion, each figure is moved a tiny bit after every photo. If you play the photos quickly one after another, it seems to move.
22402.m: In stop motion, movement is created from many single photos.

22403.e: Hayao Miyazaki’s film won the Oscar for best animated film in 2003. It tells the story of a girl in a world full of spirits.
22403.m: Hayao Miyazaki is one of the best-known animation directors in the world.

22404.q: What is the name of Elsa’s sister in the film “Frozen”?
22404.e: Anna sets out to find her sister Elsa, who has frozen the kingdom with her ice powers. The film came out in 2013.
22404.m: Anna and Elsa are the sisters from “Frozen”.

22405.q: Which Swiss stop-motion film by Claude Barras was nominated for an Oscar in 2017?
22405.e: “My Life as a Courgette” (2016) tells the story of a boy in a children’s home. The film was nominated for the Oscar for best animated film.
22405.m: With “My Life as a Courgette”, Claude Barras made an award-winning Swiss animated film.

22406.q: What is the name of the 1928 cartoon in which Mickey Mouse whistles at the wheel of a steamboat?
22406.e: “Steamboat Willie” was one of the first cartoons with synchronised sound. In it Mickey steers a steamboat until Captain Pete chases him off the bridge.
22406.m: Mickey Mouse became famous in 1928 with “Steamboat Willie”.

22407.q: What kind of animal is Gromit in the plasticine films “Wallace & Gromit”?
22407.e: Gromit is the clever dog of the inventor Wallace. He never speaks, but shows what he thinks with his eyes and forehead.

22408.q: Which film was the first to win the Oscar for best animated film in 2002?
22408.e: The category of best animated film was introduced in 2002. “Shrek” beat “Monsters, Inc.” and “Jimmy Neutron”.
22408.m: “Shrek” was the first winner of the Oscar for best animated film.

22409.q: Who is in charge of filming and tells the actors how to act?
22409.e: The director decides how the story is told and acted. The producer, on the other hand, mainly takes care of money and organisation.
22409.m: The director is in artistic charge of the filming.

22410.q: What is the text called in which the plot, scenes and dialogue of a film are written down?
22410.e: The script says who says what and what happens in each scene. It is the basis for filming.
22410.m: The script contains all the scenes and dialogue of a film.

22411.q: What do you call a series of drawn sketches that shows the individual shots before filming?
22411.e: A storyboard looks like a comic of the planned film. That way the team knows in advance what each shot should look like.
22411.m: A storyboard shows the film in advance as a series of drawings.

22412.q: What is a green background (green screen) used for when filming?
a: It is later replaced by another picture
It muffles the sound in the studio
It protects the camera from light
22412.e: The computer recognises the green colour and swaps it for any background. That way actors can seem to be in space or on a dragon.
22412.m: With a green screen you can swap the background afterwards.

22413.q: Why is the clapperboard snapped shut before a take?
a: So that picture and sound match up later
So that the actors calm down
So that the studio lights come on
22413.e: The clap can be heard in the sound and the snapping can be seen in the picture. During editing, both are lined up exactly. The scene and take number are also written on the clapperboard.
22413.m: The clapperboard helps fit picture and sound together exactly.

22414.q: What is the work called in which the filmed shots are chosen and put together into a film?
22414.e: In film editing, the editor chooses the best shots and puts them in order. This creates the film’s pace and suspense.
22414.m: In film editing, many shots become a finished film.

22415.q: What is it called when voice actors record a foreign film again in another language?
22415.e: In dubbing, voice actors speak the dialogue again to match the lip movements. With subtitles, on the other hand, the original sound stays.
22415.m: Dubbing puts a film into another language.

22416.q: What is the selection process called in which actors try out for a role?
22416.e: At a casting, applicants show how they would play a role. Then the team decides who gets the part.
22416.m: At a casting, the actors for a film are chosen.

22417.q: What are the people called who film dangerous scenes instead of the actors?
22417.e: Stunt performers are specially trained for falls, fights or car chases. Extras, on the other hand, are people in the background.
22417.m: Stunt performers take on the dangerous scenes in a film.

22418.q: What is a short advert called that shows clips from a new cinema film?
22418.e: A trailer is meant to make people curious about the film and is shown in cinemas or online before the film comes out. The end credits, on the other hand, show the names of those involved at the end.
22418.m: A trailer uses short clips to make you want to see a new film.

22419.q: Who wrote the books on which the “Harry Potter” films were based?
22419.e: The British author J. K. Rowling published seven books from 1997 to 2007. All of them were filmed between 2001 and 2011.
22419.m: The “Harry Potter” books are by J. K. Rowling.

22420.q: Which Swiss writer wrote the often-filmed “Heidi” books?
22420.e: Johanna Spyri published “Heidi’s Years of Learning and Travel” in 1880. The story has been translated into many languages and filmed again and again.

22421.q: In which country were Peter Jackson’s “The Lord of the Rings” films mainly shot?
22421.e: Peter Jackson comes from New Zealand and used the landscapes of his homeland for Middle-earth. The books were written by J. R. R. Tolkien.
22421.m: Middle-earth was filmed in New Zealand.

22422.q: Which country did Astrid Lindgren come from, whose books such as “Pippi Longstocking” have often been filmed?
22422.e: Astrid Lindgren lived in Sweden and wrote, among others, “Pippi Longstocking”, “Emil of Lönneberga” and “Ronia, the Robber’s Daughter”. Many of them were filmed in Sweden.
22422.m: Astrid Lindgren was a Swedish children’s author.

22423.q: Which German author wrote “The Neverending Story”, which was filmed in 1984?
22423.e: Michael Ende published the novel in 1979. In the film, Atreyu rides the luckdragon Falkor.
22423.m: “The Neverending Story” is by Michael Ende.

22424.q: How are Lisa and Lottie related in Erich Kästner’s often-filmed book “Lottie and Lisa”?
22424.e: The two girls meet by chance at a holiday home and realise they are twins. They swap places to bring their separated parents back together. The book was written by Erich Kästner.
22424.m: Lisa and Lottie are twins who were separated after birth.

22425.q: In the first Narnia film, through which object do the children get into the land of Narnia?
22425.e: At the back of an old wardrobe, Lucy discovers a snowy forest. The book by C. S. Lewis was filmed in 2005.
22425.m: You get into Narnia through a wardrobe.

22426.q: What is the name of the factory owner in Roald Dahl’s “Charlie and the Chocolate Factory”?
22426.e: Willy Wonka invites five children with golden tickets into his mysterious factory. The book was filmed in 1971 and 2005.
22426.m: Willy Wonka owns the famous chocolate factory.

22427.q: Which Swiss children’s book character from the Engadine was filmed in 2015 and looks for a big bell for Chalandamarz?
22427.e: The picture book “A Bell for Ursli” by Selina Chönz and Alois Carigiet came out in 1945. Xavier Koller filmed the story in 2015.
22427.m: Ursli is a famous children’s book character from the Engadine.

22428.q: Which author wrote “The Jungle Book”, which Disney made into a cartoon in 1967?
22428.e: Rudyard Kipling published the stories about the boy Mowgli in 1894. He was born in India, where the story is set.
22428.m: “The Jungle Book” is by Rudyard Kipling.

22429.q: Which country do the Asterix and Obelix comics come from?
22429.e: René Goscinny and Albert Uderzo created Asterix in France in 1959. The stories are set in a Gaulish village in Roman times.
22429.m: Asterix is a comic hero from France.

22430.q: Which Belgian artist created “The Adventures of Tintin”?
22430.e: Hergé’s real name was Georges Remi. His pen name comes from his initials R. G. pronounced in French.

22431.q: Which comic character is said to shoot faster than his own shadow?
22431.e: Lucky Luke is a lonesome cowboy in the Wild West. The Belgian artist Morris created him in 1946.
22431.m: Lucky Luke is the cowboy who draws faster than his shadow.

22433.q: Which planet does the comic hero Superman come from?
22433.e: As a baby, Superman was sent to Earth from his dying home planet Krypton. He first appeared in a comic book in 1938.
22433.m: Superman comes from the planet Krypton.

22434.q: Which comic writer created the character Spider-Man together with Steve Ditko?
22434.e: Stan Lee and Steve Ditko introduced Spider-Man in 1962. Behind the mask is the school pupil Peter Parker.
22434.m: Stan Lee helped create many famous superheroes.

22435.q: What is the shape in a comic called that shows what a character says?
22435.e: The speech bubble usually has a little point that shows which character is speaking. Thoughts are often shown in cloud-shaped bubbles.
22435.m: The speech bubble shows what a comic character says.

22436.q: In which direction is a Japanese manga traditionally read?
22436.e: Like Japanese books, manga are read from back to front and from right to left. Many translations keep this reading direction.
22436.m: A manga is read from right to left.

22437.q: What is the name of the city where Donald Duck and Scrooge McDuck live?
22437.e: The English name of the city is Duckburg. The German translator Erika Fuchs called it Entenhausen.

22438.q: Who drew the comic strip “Peanuts” with Snoopy and Charlie Brown?
22438.e: Charles M. Schulz drew “Peanuts” entirely on his own from 1950 to 2000. The strip appeared in thousands of newspapers worldwide.
22438.m: Snoopy and Charlie Brown were created by Charles M. Schulz.

22439.q: Which sport does the early 1972 video game “Pong” imitate?
22439.e: In “Pong”, two players each move a bar up and down and hit a dot back and forth. It was one of the first commercially successful arcade machines.
22439.m: “Pong” is an early video game based on table tennis.

22440.q: In which country was the game “Tetris” invented in 1984?
22440.e: The programmer Alexey Pajitnov developed “Tetris” in Moscow. You have to turn falling blocks so that full rows are formed.
22440.m: “Tetris” was invented in the Soviet Union.

22441.q: What was the game character Mario’s original job?
22441.e: Mario appeared in “Donkey Kong” in 1981 and became a plumber travelling through pipes in “Mario Bros.” (1983). His brother is called Luigi.
22441.m: Mario is a plumber by trade.

22442.q: For which company did Shigeru Miyamoto create the game characters Mario and Link?
22442.e: Shigeru Miyamoto has worked at Nintendo since 1977. Among other things, he created “Super Mario Bros.” and “The Legend of Zelda”.
22442.m: Mario and Link are Nintendo characters by Shigeru Miyamoto.

22443.q: Who chases Pac-Man around his maze?
22443.e: In the 1980 game, four coloured ghosts chase the yellow game character. After eating a power pellet, Pac-Man can turn the tables.
22443.m: Pac-Man has to flee from ghosts in the maze.

22444.q: What was special about Nintendo’s Game Boy, which came out in 1989?
a: It only worked on the TV
22444.e: The Game Boy was a portable games console with batteries and a small screen. Together with “Tetris” it sold extremely well.
22444.m: The Game Boy was a console for playing on the go.

22445.q: What type is the Pokémon Pikachu?
22445.e: Pikachu stores electricity in its red cheeks and attacks with lightning. The first Pokémon games came out in Japan in 1996.

22446.q: Which country does the game “Minecraft” come from?
22446.e: The Swedish programmer Markus Persson began developing it in 2009, and his company Mojang is based in Stockholm. In “Minecraft” you build worlds out of blocks.

22447.q: What were the first home games consoles connected to in the 1970s?
22447.e: The first home console, the Magnavox Odyssey from 1972, was connected to the television. A plastic sheet with the playing field was placed over the screen.
22447.m: The first home consoles ran on the television.

22448.q: What are video game machines called that people used to play with coins, mainly in amusement arcades?
22448.e: Arcade machines were very popular in the 1970s and 1980s. Many well-known games first came out as arcade machines and only later for consoles.
22448.m: Arcade machines are video games in amusement arcades.

22449.q: Which genre does a game belong to in which the character mainly jumps over platforms and obstacles?
22449.e: Such games are also called platformers or “jump and run” games. The character runs through levels and jumps over gaps and enemies.
22449.m: In a platform game the character jumps and runs through the levels.

22450.q: Which genre does the game “Mario Kart” belong to?
22450.e: In “Mario Kart”, characters race each other in little go-karts and collect items along the way. Light-hearted racing games like this are also called kart racers.

22451.q: Which genre does “Tetris” belong to, in which you cleverly arrange falling blocks?
22451.e: Puzzle games are about logic, skill and spatial thinking. You have to arrange shapes or pieces so that a task is solved.

22452.q: What does the abbreviation RPG stand for in computer games?
22452.e: In an RPG, or role-playing game, the character collects experience points and becomes stronger during the game.
22452.m: An RPG is a role-playing game in which the character develops.

22453.q: Which genre does a game like “SimCity”, in which you plan and run a city, belong to?
22453.e: In city-building games you put up houses, roads and services and have to manage your money and resources. If you plan well, the city grows.
22453.m: In a city-building game you plan and run a city or a realm.

22454.q: What do you call games with a large game world you can explore freely without a fixed route?
22454.e: In an open world, players decide for themselves where to go and which tasks to do first.
22454.m: In an open-world game you can explore the game world freely.

22455.q: In which genre do you mainly solve puzzles, collect items and talk to characters, often by clicking the mouse?
22455.e: In point-and-click adventures you point at things in the picture with the mouse and click. You often have to combine items cleverly to get further.
22455.m: In an adventure you make progress with puzzles and conversations.

22456.q: What is the difference between a turn-based strategy game and a real-time strategy game?
22456.e: In turn-based games you take your turn one after the other, a bit like chess. In real-time strategy games everyone acts at the same time.
22456.m: In a turn-based game each player takes a turn in order.

22457.q: What do you do in a rhythm game?
a: Make inputs in time with the music
22457.e: In rhythm games you have to press buttons, dance or clap exactly when the music calls for it. The more precisely you hit the beat, the more points you get.
22457.m: A rhythm game asks for inputs in time with the music.

22458.q: What do you call games that are mainly meant to teach knowledge, for example in maths or learning vocabulary?
22458.e: Learning games combine fun with practice, for example through points, levels or rewards. Quiz apps are also part of this.
22458.m: Learning games help you learn new things in a playful way.

22459.q: Who invented printing with movable metal letters in Mainz around 1450?
22459.e: Johannes Gutenberg cast single letters out of metal, which could be put together again and again. This made it possible to produce books much faster and more cheaply.
22459.m: Gutenberg’s printing made books available to many people.

22460.q: Which invention from 1876 made it possible to send the human voice along wires?
22460.e: Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone in 1876. For the first time, people could talk directly to each other over long distances.
22460.m: Since 1876 the telephone has carried the voice along wires.

22461.q: At which research centre in Geneva was the World Wide Web invented in 1989?
22461.e: In 1989, the British physicist Tim Berners-Lee proposed a system of linked pages at CERN. This became the World Wide Web.
22461.m: The World Wide Web was invented at CERN in Geneva.

22462.q: When was the oldest surviving photograph taken by Joseph Nicéphore Niépce?
22462.e: Niépce photographed the view from his window in France. The exposure took many hours back then.
22462.m: The oldest surviving photograph is about 200 years old.

22463.q: Which of these media has existed the longest?
22463.e: Printed newspapers have existed for around 400 years. Radio and television only came in the 20th century, and the internet even later.
22463.m: The newspaper is older than radio, television and the internet.

22464.q: How were the first radio broadcasts brought to people?
a: By radio waves through the air
22464.e: Radio works with invisible radio waves. In 1901 the Italian Guglielmo Marconi sent radio signals across the Atlantic for the first time.
22464.m: Radio transmits sounds with radio waves.

22465.q: In which decade did the compact disc (CD) for music come on the market?
22465.e: The first music CDs were sold in 1982. They gradually replaced records and music cassettes.
22465.m: The CD was introduced in the 1980s.

22466.q: What does streaming mean for films and music?
a: Content is played while it is being transmitted
Films are burned onto a DVD
Programmes only come through the aerial
22466.e: With streaming, a file does not first have to be downloaded completely. The data keeps arriving over the internet and is played straight away.
22466.m: With streaming you watch or listen to content directly over the internet.

22467.q: Which Swiss daily newspaper has been published since 1780 and is one of the oldest newspapers in the world still being published?
22467.e: The newspaper was founded in 1780 as the “Zürcher Zeitung” and has been called the “Neue Zürcher Zeitung” since 1821. It is one of the oldest newspapers in Switzerland.
22467.m: The “Neue Zürcher Zeitung” has been published since 1780.

22468.q: What is the code of short and long signals that was used to send messages by telegraph called?
22468.e: Morse code goes back to Samuel Morse and was used from the 1840s. The well-known distress signal SOS is three short, three long, three short.
22468.m: Morse code sent messages as short and long signals.

22516.q: A cinema sells 240 tickets at 18 francs each in one evening, and half the takings go to the film distributor. How much does the distributor get?
22516.e: 240 · 18 = 4320 francs in takings. Half of that is 4320 : 2 = 2160 francs.
22516.m: The cinema and the distributor share the ticket takings by an agreed proportion.

22568.q: What colour do you get when you mix red and white?
22568.e: White makes colours lighter. Red turns into a light red, which we call pink.
22568.m: Red with lots of white turns pink.

22569.q: What colour is the sky on a clear day?
22569.e: Sunlight is spread out in the air. Blue light is scattered the most, which is why the sky looks blue.
22569.m: In fine weather the sky is blue.

22570.q: What colour do you get when you mix black and white?
22570.e: Black and white together make grey. With more white, the grey gets lighter.
22570.m: Black and white together make grey.

22571.q: How many colours do people usually count in a rainbow?
22571.e: A rainbow appears when sunlight shines through raindrops. People usually count seven colours, from red to violet.
22571.m: A rainbow usually has seven colours.

22572.q: How many sides does a square have?
22572.e: A square has four sides. All four sides are the same length.
22572.m: A square has four sides of equal length.

22573.q: How many corners does a hexagon have?
22573.e: A hexagon has six corners. The cells of a honeycomb have this shape.

22574.q: What shape is each face of a dice?
22574.e: A dice has six faces. Each face is a square.
22574.m: Each face of a dice is a square.

22575.q: What do you call a shape that is completely round, like a ball?
22575.e: A sphere is round on all sides. A ball or a marble has this shape.
22575.m: A ball has the shape of a sphere.

22576.q: What shape is a stop sign?
22576.e: The stop sign is a red octagon with eight corners. That way you can recognise it even from behind.
22576.m: The stop sign is a red octagon.

22580.q: How many legs do two dogs have altogether?
22580.e: A dog has 4 legs. Two dogs have 4 + 4 = 8 legs.
22580.m: Two dogs have eight legs altogether.

22582.q: What is a baby cow called?
22582.e: A baby cow is called a calf. A foal is a young horse.
22582.m: A cow's baby is called a calf.

22583.q: How many legs does a beetle have?
22583.e: Beetles are insects. All insects have six legs.
22583.m: Insects such as beetles have six legs.

22584.q: Which animal in the Alps hibernates for a long time in winter?
22584.e: The marmot sleeps for many months in winter in its burrow underground. The ibex and the chamois stay awake in winter.
22584.m: The marmot sleeps through the winter in its burrow.

22585.q: What do fish use to breathe underwater?
22585.e: Fish take oxygen out of the water with their gills. They use their fins for swimming.

22586.q: Which of these animals lays eggs?
22586.e: Hens are birds and lay eggs. Cows, horses and sheep give birth to live young.

22587.q: Besides water, what does a plant need to grow?
22587.e: Plants need sunlight. With light, water and air they make their own food.
22587.m: Plants need light and water to grow.

22588.q: Which part of a plant is usually in the soil?
22588.e: The root holds the plant firmly in the ground. It also takes up water from the soil.
22588.m: The root holds the plant in the soil.

22589.q: Which tree do acorns grow on?
22589.e: Acorns are the fruit of the oak tree. Squirrels and wild boar love to eat them.
22589.m: Acorns grow on the oak tree.

22590.q: Which flower is a well-known symbol of the Alps?
22590.e: Edelweiss grows high up in the mountains. It has white, felt-like flowers and is protected in Switzerland.
22590.m: Edelweiss is the famous flower of the Alps.

22591.q: Which tree stays green in winter too?
22591.e: The fir tree has needles that it keeps in winter. Beech, oak and maple lose their leaves in autumn.
22591.m: The fir tree stays green even in winter.

22592.q: Which plant has lots of spines and often grows in the desert?
22592.e: The cactus stores water in its thick stem. Its spines protect it from animals.
22592.m: The cactus stores water and has spines.

22593.q: Which country is the city of Paris in?
22593.e: Paris is the capital of France. France is one of Switzerland's neighbours.
22593.m: Paris is the capital of France.

22594.q: In which city do the Swiss Federal Council and Parliament work?
22594.e: Bern is the federal city of Switzerland. The Federal Palace is there.
22594.m: The Swiss government works in Bern.

22595.q: Which country is a neighbour of Switzerland?
22595.e: Switzerland has five neighbouring countries: Germany, France, Italy, Austria and Liechtenstein.
22595.m: Austria is a neighbour of Switzerland.

22596.q: In which country do kangaroos live in the wild?
22596.e: In the wild, kangaroos are found only in Australia and on a few nearby islands.
22596.m: Kangaroos live in the wild in Australia.

22597.q: Which language do people speak in Italy?
22597.e: People in Italy speak Italian. Italian is also spoken in Ticino, a Swiss canton.

22598.q: Which country is the city of Tokyo in?
22598.e: Tokyo is the capital of Japan. Japan is made up of many islands.
22598.m: Tokyo is the capital of Japan.

22599.q: What shape is the Swiss national flag?
22599.e: The Swiss national flag is square. Only very few countries have a flag like this, for example the Vatican.

22600.q: What can you see in the middle of the Swiss flag?
22600.e: In the middle of the red Swiss flag there is a white cross. It is the symbol of Switzerland.
22600.m: The Swiss flag shows a white cross.

22601.q: Which country has a flag with a red circle on a white background?
22601.e: The red circle on Japan's flag stands for the sun. Japan is also called the Land of the Rising Sun.
22601.m: Japan's flag shows a red sun.

22602.q: What colours is the flag of Italy?
22602.e: The flag of Italy has three vertical stripes in green, white and red.
22602.m: The Italian flag is green, white and red.

22603.q: Which country has a black, red and gold flag?
22603.e: The flag of Germany has three horizontal stripes in black, red and gold. The flag of Austria is red, white and red.
22603.m: The German flag is black, red and gold.

22604.q: Which flag shows a circle of twelve yellow stars on blue?
22604.e: The flag of Europe is blue with twelve yellow stars in a circle. The number twelve stands for completeness.
22604.m: The flag of Europe has twelve yellow stars in a circle.

22605.q: Who bakes fresh bread every morning?
22605.e: The baker bakes bread, croissants and plaited Swiss loaves. Bakers often start work in the middle of the night.

22606.q: Who brings letters and parcels to our homes?
22606.e: The postman works for the post office. He puts letters and parcels in the letterboxes.
22606.m: The postman brings letters and parcels.

22607.q: How many wheels does a bike have?
22607.e: A bike has two wheels, one at the front and one at the back. A tricycle has three.

22608.e: A train runs on rails. In Switzerland, lots of people travel by train.

22609.q: Which vehicle flies with a big propeller on its roof?
22609.e: A helicopter has a big spinning rotor on top. With it, it can take off straight up and hover in the air.
22609.m: The helicopter flies with a rotor on its roof.

22610.e: A submarine can dive and travel underwater. Its name means ‘under the sea’.

22611.q: What colour are the PostBuses in Switzerland?
22611.e: The PostBuses in Switzerland are yellow. They even go to small mountain villages.

22612.q: What do you call a railway whose cabin travels through the air on a cable?
22612.e: On a cable car, the cabin hangs from a cable. It gets you up a mountain quickly.
22612.m: On a cable car, the cabin hangs from a cable.

22613.q: Which boat is powered by the wind?
22613.e: A sailing boat catches the wind in its sail. That way it moves forward without an engine.
22613.m: The sailing boat moves using the power of the wind.

22614.q: Which vehicle flies all the way into space?
22614.e: A rocket is very powerful and fast. It can fly all the way into space.

22615.e: Cheese is made from milk, for example cow's milk. Switzerland is famous for its cheese.

22616.e: Chocolate is made from cocoa beans. Cocoa grows on trees in warm countries.
22616.m: Chocolate is made from cocoa beans.

22617.q: Which Swiss dish do you eat from a pot of melted cheese?
22617.e: With fondue, you dip pieces of bread into melted cheese using a long fork.
22617.m: With fondue, you dip bread into cheese.

22618.q: Which vegetable is rösti made from?
22618.e: For rösti, you grate potatoes and fry them in a pan until they are crispy.
22618.m: Rösti is made from grated potatoes.

22619.q: Which bread do people in Switzerland often eat for breakfast on Sundays?
22619.e: Zopf is a plaited bread made with butter, milk and flour. Many families eat it on Sundays.
22619.m: On Sundays there is often a Zopf.

22620.e: Bees collect nectar from flowers. They turn it into honey in the beehive.

22621.q: When do people in Switzerland eat their ‘Znüni’?
22621.e: The Znüni is a small snack in the morning, at about nine o'clock. Many children eat it at break time at school.
22621.m: The Znüni is eaten in the morning.

22622.q: In which country are the pyramids of Giza?
22622.e: The pyramids of Giza are in Egypt. They are over 4000 years old.
22622.m: The pyramids of Giza are in Egypt.

22623.q: What is the very long wall in China called?
22623.e: The Great Wall of China is many thousands of kilometres long. It was built a long time ago for protection.
22623.m: The Great Wall of China is very long.

22624.q: Which large statue in New York holds up a torch?
22624.e: The Statue of Liberty stands on a small island in New York harbour. It was a gift from France to the USA.
22624.m: The Statue of Liberty holds up a torch.

22625.q: In which city is there a famous leaning tower?
22625.e: The tower of Pisa in Italy leans because the ground beneath it is soft.
22625.m: The leaning tower is in Pisa.

22626.q: Which mountain is the highest in the world?
22626.e: Mount Everest in the Himalayas is about 8849 metres high. No mountain on Earth is higher.
22626.m: Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.

22627.q: Which animal is the largest in the world?
22627.e: The blue whale can grow to about 30 metres long. It is the largest animal living on Earth today.
22627.m: The blue whale is the largest animal in the world.

22628.q: Which land animal is the tallest?
22628.e: A giraffe can grow over five metres tall. With its long neck it reaches leaves high up in the trees.
22628.m: The giraffe is the tallest animal on land.

22629.q: Which land animal runs the fastest?
22629.e: For a short time, the cheetah can run at about 100 kilometres per hour. No other land animal is that fast.
22629.m: The cheetah is the fastest land animal.

22630.q: Which ocean is the largest in the world?
22630.e: The Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean. It is bigger than all the land on Earth put together.
22630.m: The Pacific is the largest ocean.

22632.q: What do you use to brush your teeth?
22632.e: You brush your teeth with a toothbrush and toothpaste. You should do it at least twice a day.
22632.m: You brush your teeth with a toothbrush.

22633.q: What do you use to cut paper?
22633.e: You can cut paper with scissors. You stick it together with glue.

22634.e: A clock shows the hours and minutes. Scales, on the other hand, measure weight.

22635.q: What do you take with you to stay dry in the rain?
22635.e: An umbrella keeps the rain off. That way you stay dry.
22635.m: An umbrella protects you from the rain.

22636.q: What do you use to unlock a front door?
22636.e: You open the lock of the door with a key. Without the right key, the door stays shut.
22636.m: You unlock the door with a key.

22637.q: Where does food stay cool and fresh?
22637.e: It is cold inside the fridge. That is why milk, cheese and meat do not go off so quickly there.
22637.m: Food stays cool in the fridge.

22638.q: What gets wet while it dries?
22638.e: You dry yourself with a towel. It soaks up the water and gets wet itself.
22638.m: A towel gets wet when you dry yourself.

22639.q: What has teeth but cannot bite?
22639.e: A comb has lots of prongs, which are called teeth. But it cannot bite with them.
22639.m: A comb has teeth but does not bite.

22640.q: What has a bed but never sleeps?
22640.e: The ground a river flows along is called a riverbed. But a river cannot sleep.
22640.m: A river has a bed but never sleeps.

22641.q: Anna's mother has three children: Lena, Tim and who else?
22641.e: The question talks about Anna's mother. So Anna herself is the third child.
22641.m: With riddles, you need to read carefully.

22642.q: Which is heavier, a kilo of feathers or a kilo of stones?
22642.e: A kilo always weighs the same. The feathers just take up much more space.
22642.m: A kilo of feathers weighs the same as a kilo of stones.

22643.q: Riddle: Which months have at least 28 days?
22643.e: Every month has at least 28 days. February has 28 or 29 days, the other months have 30 or 31.
22643.m: Every month has at least twenty-eight days.

22644.q: What has four legs but cannot walk?
22644.e: A table usually has four legs. But it just stands still and cannot walk.
22644.m: A table has legs but cannot walk.

22645.q: Which building is the tallest in the world at 828 metres (as of 2026)?
22645.e: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai opened in 2010 and is 828 m tall. The Jeddah Tower in Saudi Arabia is meant to beat it, but in 2026 it is still being built.
22645.m: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai is the tallest building in the world.

22646.q: Which sprinter has held the 100 metres world record of 9.58 seconds since 2009 (as of 2026)?
22646.e: The Jamaican Usain Bolt ran 9.58 seconds at the 2009 World Championships in Berlin. Nobody has run faster since.
22646.m: Usain Bolt holds the 100 metres world record with 9.58 seconds.

22647.q: Which time barrier did the Kenyan Sabastian Sawe become the first person to break in an official race, at the 2026 London Marathon?
22647.e: Sabastian Sawe ran 1:59:30 in London in April 2026. That made him the first person to finish under two hours in an official race.
22647.m: Since 2026, the men's marathon world record has been under two hours.

22648.q: Which swimmer won 28 Olympic medals, more than any other athlete (as of 2026)?
22648.e: Michael Phelps from the USA won a total of 28 Olympic medals between 2004 and 2016, 23 of them gold. That is still a record.
22648.m: Michael Phelps is the most successful Olympian of all time.

22649.q: Which tunnel, about 57 km long, is the longest railway tunnel in the world (as of 2026)?
22649.e: The Gotthard Base Tunnel opened in 2016 and is about 57 km long. It links Erstfeld in the canton of Uri with Bodio in Ticino.
22649.m: The longest railway tunnel in the world runs under the Gotthard in Switzerland.

22650.q: Which country has the longest bridge in the world, a railway viaduct about 165 km long (as of 2026)?
22650.e: The Danyang Kunshan Grand Bridge is a viaduct on the Beijing to Shanghai high-speed line. It is about 165 km long and opened in 2011.
22650.m: The longest bridge in the world is a railway viaduct in China.

22651.q: Which Swiss man, together with Brian Jones, made the first non-stop balloon flight around the world in 1999?
22651.e: In 1999 Bertrand Piccard and Brian Jones flew round the Earth in the balloon “Breitling Orbiter 3” in just under 20 days. They had set off from Château-d'Oex in the canton of Vaud.
22651.m: The first non-stop balloon flight round the world started in Switzerland.

22652.q: In which sport has the Cuban Javier Sotomayor held the world record of 2.45 m since 1993?
22652.e: In 1993 in Salamanca, Javier Sotomayor cleared the bar at 2.45 m. In the long jump and triple jump you jump much further, and in the pole vault much higher.
22652.m: The men's high jump world record is 2.45 metres.

22653.q: In which Swiss city did Albert Einstein work at the patent office when he published his special theory of relativity in 1905?
22653.e: Einstein worked at the Federal Office for Intellectual Property in Bern from 1902 to 1909. In 1905 he published several famous papers there.
22653.m: Albert Einstein wrote his most famous papers while working in Bern.

22654.q: Which scientist was the first person to win two Nobel Prizes?
22654.e: Marie Curie won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 and the one in Chemistry in 1911. She studied radioactivity.
22654.m: Marie Curie won Nobel Prizes in two different sciences.

22655.q: Which organisation did Henri Dunant from Geneva found?
22655.e: In 1859 Henri Dunant saw the suffering of the wounded after the Battle of Solferino. He inspired the founding of the Red Cross and received the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.
22655.m: Henri Dunant from Geneva is the founder of the Red Cross.

22656.q: In which city was Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart born in 1756?
22656.e: Mozart was born in Salzburg in 1756. Even as a child he composed music and toured Europe as a child prodigy.
22656.m: Mozart came from Salzburg in Austria.

22657.q: Which composer wrote the 9th Symphony when he was already almost completely deaf?
22657.e: From about the age of 30, Beethoven slowly lost his hearing. Even so, he kept composing, including the 9th Symphony with the “Ode to Joy”.
22657.m: Beethoven composed great works even though he was deaf.

22658.q: Who became the youngest person to win the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, at the age of 17?
22658.e: Malala Yousafzai from Pakistan campaigns for girls' right to education. She won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014 at the age of 17.
22658.m: Malala Yousafzai fights for all girls to be allowed to go to school.

22659.q: Who became South Africa's first black president in 1994, after spending 27 years in prison?
22659.e: Nelson Mandela fought against apartheid, the system of racial segregation in South Africa. After his release in 1990 he became president in 1994.
22659.m: Nelson Mandela became a symbol of the fight against racial segregation.

22660.q: How many Grand Slam singles titles did the Basel tennis player Roger Federer win?
22660.e: Roger Federer won a total of 20 Grand Slam titles between 2003 and 2018, eight of them at Wimbledon. He retired in 2022.
22660.m: Roger Federer won Wimbledon eight times.

22661.q: Which Swiss author wrote the story of “Heidi”?
22661.e: Johanna Spyri published the first Heidi book in 1880. It has been translated into many languages and is known all over the world.
22661.m: The Heidi stories were written by Johanna Spyri from Zurich.

22662.q: Which Renaissance artist painted the “Mona Lisa” and also drew flying machines?
22662.e: Leonardo da Vinci was a painter, inventor and scientist. The “Mona Lisa” now hangs in the Louvre in Paris.
22662.m: Leonardo da Vinci was both an artist and an inventor.

22663.q: How did Bertrand Piccard and André Borschberg travel round the Earth in 2015 and 2016?
22663.e: The aircraft “Solar Impulse 2” flew around the world using only solar energy. The journey, in several stages, ended in Abu Dhabi in July 2016.
22663.m: Solar Impulse showed that a plane can fly round the world on solar power alone.

22664.q: Which plant gave the Swiss George de Mestral the idea for Velcro?
22664.e: After a walk, burdock burrs were stuck in his dog's fur. Under the microscope, de Mestral saw the tiny hooks and copied them.
22664.m: Velcro is a Swiss invention modelled on nature.

22665.q: Which company from Ibach in the canton of Schwyz makes the famous Swiss Army knife?
22665.e: At the end of 1891, Karl Elsener in Ibach took over making soldiers' knives for the Swiss Army. His workshop became the company Victorinox, which today sells pocket knives all over the world.
22665.m: The famous Swiss Army knife comes from the canton of Schwyz.

22666.q: In which country was milk chocolate invented in 1875?
22666.e: In 1875 Daniel Peter from western Switzerland mixed cocoa and sugar with condensed milk. His friend Henri Nestlé helped him.
22666.m: Daniel Peter made milk chocolate from western Switzerland famous worldwide.

22667.q: At which research centre did Tim Berners-Lee invent the World Wide Web in 1989?
22667.e: Tim Berners-Lee wanted researchers to be able to share their data easily. At CERN near Geneva he developed web pages, links and the first browser for this.
22667.m: The World Wide Web was invented in Switzerland.

22668.q: Who patented the first petrol-powered car in 1886?
22668.e: In 1886 Carl Benz patented his three-wheeled Motorwagen. It is considered the first practical car.
22668.m: The world's first car had only three wheels.

22669.q: Who made the first controlled powered flight in history in 1903?
22669.e: Orville and Wilbur Wright flew their “Flyer” in the USA on 17 December 1903. The first flight lasted only 12 seconds.
22669.m: In 1903 the Wright brothers started the age of the aeroplane.

22670.q: Which forerunner of the bicycle did Karl Drais invent in 1817?
22670.e: The running machine had two wheels but no pedals. You pushed yourself along the ground with your feet.
22670.m: The first two-wheeler had no pedals yet.

22671.q: In which country did people invent paper?
22671.e: People in China already made paper more than 2000 years ago. Around the year 105, the official Cai Lun greatly improved how it was made.
22671.m: Paper is an invention from ancient China.

22672.q: Which invention made Alfred Nobel rich, whose fortune now pays for the Nobel Prizes?
22672.e: The Swede Alfred Nobel invented dynamite in 1867. In his will he decided that prizes should be awarded every year with his money.
22672.m: The Nobel Prizes are paid for from the fortune of the inventor of dynamite.

22673.q: For what occasion did Paris build the Eiffel Tower in 1889?
22673.e: The Eiffel Tower served as the entrance gate to the 1889 World's Fair in Paris. It was actually meant to be pulled down again after 20 years.
22673.m: The Eiffel Tower was originally only meant for an exhibition.

22674.q: In which country is the Inca ruined city of Machu Picchu?
22674.e: Machu Picchu lies high in the Andes of Peru. The Incas built the city in the 15th century.
22674.m: Machu Picchu is the most famous Inca city, in Peru.

22675.q: Why did the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan have the Taj Mahal built in India?
a: As a tomb for his wife
22675.e: Shah Jahan had the white marble building put up for his late wife Mumtaz Mahal. It was finished around 1648.
22675.m: The Taj Mahal is a tomb made of white marble.

22676.q: What took place in the Colosseum in ancient Rome?
22676.e: The Colosseum opened in the year 80 and held about 50,000 spectators. Gladiators fought there and there were animal hunts.
22676.m: In ancient Rome, gladiators fought in the Colosseum.

22677.q: What is the name of Europe's highest railway station, at 3454 metres above sea level?
22677.e: The Jungfrau Railway runs through a tunnel in the Eiger and Mönch up to the Jungfraujoch. It was completed in 1912.
22677.m: Europe's highest railway station is in the Bernese Oberland.

22678.q: Which covered wooden bridge with a water tower is the landmark of Lucerne?
22678.e: Chapel Bridge was built in the 14th century and is one of the oldest wooden bridges in Europe. In 1993 much of it burned down and it was rebuilt.
22678.m: Chapel Bridge with its water tower is the landmark of Lucerne.

22679.q: Which lake is the famous Chillon Castle near Montreux on?
22679.e: Chillon Castle stands on a rock in Lake Geneva. It is one of the most visited historic monuments in Switzerland.
22679.m: Chillon Castle stands right on the shore of Lake Geneva.

22680.q: What exactly does the name “Big Ben” in London refer to?
a: The largest bell in the tower
The river next to the tower
22680.e: “Big Ben” is really the nickname of the great bell. Since 2012 the tower itself has been called the “Elizabeth Tower”.
22680.m: Big Ben is really the name of a bell.

22681.q: Which statement about the Great Wall of China is true?
a: You cannot see it from the Moon
It was built in one year
22681.e: The wall is very long, but only a few metres wide. It cannot be seen with the naked eye from the Moon, as astronauts have confirmed.
22681.m: The idea that you can see the Great Wall of China from the Moon is a myth.

22682.q: How high is Mount Everest according to the joint survey by Nepal and China in 2020?
22682.e: In 2020 Nepal and China gave its height as 8848.86 m. That makes Mount Everest the highest mountain on Earth.
22682.m: At almost 8850 metres, Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.

22683.q: What is the name of the highest mountain peak in Switzerland?
22683.e: The Dufourspitze in the Monte Rosa massif is 4634 m high. It is named after the general and map-maker Guillaume-Henri Dufour.
22683.m: The highest peak in Switzerland is the Dufourspitze.

22684.q: Where is the deepest point of the world's oceans?
22684.e: At its deepest point, the Mariana Trench in the Pacific is almost 11,000 m deep. Mount Everest would fit inside it.
22684.m: The deepest point of the oceans is in the Mariana Trench.

22685.q: What is the largest animal that has ever lived on Earth?
22685.e: Blue whales grow over 30 m long and weigh well over 100 tonnes. They are heavier than the largest known dinosaurs.
22685.m: The blue whale is the largest animal of all time.

22687.q: Which kind of tree is “Hyperion”, the tallest known living tree in the world at about 116 m (as of 2026)?
22687.e: Hyperion grows in California and was discovered in 2006. Its exact location is kept secret to protect it.
22687.m: The tallest tree in the world is a redwood in California.

22688.q: In which country is Angel Falls, the highest waterfall on Earth at about 979 m?
22688.e: Angel Falls plunges down from a table mountain in Venezuela. It is about 40 times as high as the Rhine Falls.
22688.m: The highest waterfall in the world is in Venezuela.

22689.q: Which glacier is the largest and longest in the Alps?
22689.e: The Great Aletsch Glacier in Valais is about 20 km long. Because of global warming it melts back a little every year.
22689.m: The longest glacier in the Alps is in Valais.

22690.q: Where was the lowest air temperature ever recorded at a weather station, minus 89.2 °C, measured in 1983?
22690.e: The Russian research station Vostok lies at over 3400 m in the interior of Antarctica. A temperature of minus 89.2 °C was measured there on 21 July 1983.
22690.m: The coldest temperature ever measured comes from Antarctica.

22691.q: Which scientist described the law of gravity in the 17th century?
22691.e: Isaac Newton published his law of gravitation in 1687. According to a story, a falling apple gave him the idea.
22691.m: Isaac Newton explained why things fall to the ground.

22692.q: Which medicine did Alexander Fleming discover by chance in a mould in 1928?
22692.e: Fleming noticed that a mould in a dish was killing bacteria. This led to the first antibiotic.

22693.q: What shape of DNA did James Watson and Francis Crick describe in 1953?
22693.e: DNA is made of two strands wound around each other like a twisted rope ladder. Important X-ray images for this came from Rosalind Franklin.
22693.m: DNA has the shape of a twisted ladder.

22694.q: Which astronomer explained in the 16th century that the Earth goes round the Sun?
22694.e: Copernicus published his work in 1543. Before that, most people believed the Earth was at the centre of the universe.
22694.m: Copernicus put the Sun at the centre of our solar system.

22695.q: What did Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen discover in 1895?
a: Rays that pass through the body
22695.e: Röntgen discovered rays that make bones inside the body visible. For this he received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.
22695.m: With X-rays you can see inside the body.

22696.q: What did Galileo Galilei discover with his telescope in 1610?
22696.e: Galileo saw four bright dots circling Jupiter: Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto. This showed that not everything goes round the Earth.
22696.m: Galileo was the first to discover moons around another planet.

22697.q: What status was Pluto given in 2006?
22697.e: Pluto, discovered in 1930, had long been counted as the ninth planet. In 2006 the International Astronomical Union decided that it is a dwarf planet.
22697.m: Since 2006 Pluto has not been a planet but a dwarf planet.

22698.q: What did the Geneva astronomers Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz discover in 1995?
a: A new moon of the Earth
22698.e: They found the first planet orbiting a star like the Sun. For this they received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2019.
22698.m: The first exoplanet around a Sun-like star was discovered by researchers from Geneva.

22699.q: Which particle did scientists detect at CERN near Geneva in 2012?
22699.e: Scientists had predicted the Higgs boson back in 1964. They found it in 2012 at CERN's large particle accelerator, the LHC.
22699.m: The Higgs particle was discovered at CERN in 2012.

22700.q: Against which disease did Edward Jenner develop the first vaccination in 1796?
22700.e: Jenner vaccinated a boy with harmless cowpox, after which the boy was protected against dangerous smallpox. Since 1980 smallpox has been considered wiped out worldwide.
22700.m: The first vaccination in history protected against smallpox.

22701.q: What is Archimedes said to have shouted when he discovered buoyancy in the bath?
22701.e: “Eureka” is Greek and means “I have found it”. Archimedes realised that an object in water is pushed up as strongly as the weight of the water it pushes aside.
22701.m: An object in water is pushed upwards by as much as the displaced water weighs.

22702.q: What is burned at the Sechseläuten festival in Zurich to drive away winter?
22702.e: The Böögg is a snowman made of cotton wool and filled with fireworks. The faster its head explodes, the better the summer is supposed to be.
22702.m: At the Sechseläuten, the Böögg is burned in Zurich.

22703.q: At what time does Basel Carnival begin with the Morgestraich?
22703.e: On the Monday after Ash Wednesday, at 4 in the morning, all the lights in Basel's old town go out. Then groups called Cliques set off with lanterns, drums and piccolos.
22703.m: Basel Carnival starts in the middle of the night at four o'clock.

22704.q: What is the Indian festival of lights called, when many oil lamps are lit?
22704.e: Diwali is celebrated in autumn and stands for the victory of light over darkness. It is one of the most important festivals in Hinduism.
22704.m: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights.

22705.q: In which country do people celebrate the “Día de los Muertos” with colourful sugar skulls?
22705.e: On the Day of the Dead at the beginning of November, people in Mexico cheerfully remember those who have died. They decorate altars with flowers, photos and food.
22705.m: In Mexico, people remember the dead with a colourful festival.

22706.q: Why does Chinese New Year fall on a different date every year?
a: It is drawn by lot every year
22706.e: The traditional Chinese calendar follows the Moon and the Sun. That is why the New Year festival always falls between 21 January and 20 February.
22706.m: Chinese New Year follows the lunar calendar.

22707.q: What do people throw at each other at the Indian festival of Holi?
22707.e: Holi is a spring festival in India. People throw coloured powder and coloured water at each other.
22707.m: Holi is the festival of colours.

22708.q: What do people throw at each other at the “La Tomatina” festival in the Spanish town of Buñol?
22708.e: Since 1945 a huge tomato fight has taken place in Buñol every year at the end of August. More than 100 tonnes of ripe tomatoes are used.
22708.m: In Buñol in Spain there is a tomato fight every year.

22709.q: What do people in Japan admire during the spring custom of Hanami?
22709.e: At Hanami, families and friends have picnics under blossoming cherry trees. The blossom lasts only about a week.
22709.m: In Japan, Hanami means looking at the cherry blossom.

22710.q: On which date does Switzerland celebrate its national day?
22710.e: 1 August recalls the Federal Charter of 1291. There are bonfires on the hills, paper lanterns and fireworks.
22710.m: Switzerland celebrates its birthday on 1 August.

22711.q: What does the word “Röstigraben” mean in Switzerland?
a: The language border between German and French
A potato field in the Seeland
22711.e: The “Röstigraben” (rösti ditch) is a joking name for the border between German-speaking and French-speaking Switzerland. It often stands for different opinions in votes.
22711.m: The Röstigraben jokingly separates German-speaking Switzerland from the French-speaking part.

22712.q: When do Muslims who observe the month of Ramadan fast?
22712.e: During the fasting month of Ramadan, people do not eat or drink during the day. After sunset they meet to break the fast together.
22712.m: During Ramadan people fast in the daytime and only eat after sunset.

22713.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
22713.e: Two hearts pump blood through the gills, and a third pumps it through the rest of the body. An octopus's blood is also bluish.
22713.m: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood.

22714.q: Which food stays edible almost forever if it is stored well?
22714.e: Honey contains very little water and lots of sugar, so bacteria can hardly grow in it. Honey thousands of years old has been found in Egyptian tombs.
22714.m: Thanks to its high sugar content, honey almost never goes off.

22715.q: From a botanical point of view, what type of fruit is a banana?
22715.e: In botany, a berry is a fruit whose whole fruit wall is fleshy and which contains the seeds. The banana fits this description.
22715.m: Botanically speaking, the banana is a berry.

22716.q: What is special about the planet Venus?
a: A day lasts longer than a year
22716.e: Venus spins very slowly: one turn takes about 243 Earth days. But it takes only about 225 Earth days to go round the Sun.
22716.m: On Venus a day is longer than a year.

a: Because of colourings in their food
Because they roll in red sand
Because their blood shows through their skin
22717.e: Flamingos eat small shrimps and algae containing red colourings called carotenoids. These are stored in their feathers.
22717.m: Flamingos turn pink because of their food.

22718.q: Why is the Eiffel Tower a few centimetres taller in summer than in winter?
a: Because iron expands when it is warm
Because it is freshly painted in summer
Because the ground swells in summer
Because an aerial is added in summer
22718.e: Metal expands when it gets warm and contracts in the cold. For the iron tower, over 300 m tall, that makes a few centimetres.
22718.m: Most materials expand when they get warm.

22719.q: Which is hotter, a lightning bolt or the surface of the Sun?
22719.e: A lightning bolt briefly heats the air to about 30,000 °C. The surface of the Sun is about 5500 °C.
22719.m: For a moment, lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun.

22720.q: Which animals already existed on Earth before the first trees?
22720.e: The first sharks lived over 400 million years ago. The first trees only appeared about 385 million years ago.

22721.q: Which event did the Egyptian queen Cleopatra live closer to in time?
a: The building of the Great Pyramid of Khufu
22721.e: Cleopatra died in 30 BC. The Moon landing came about 2000 years later, but the Great Pyramid was built around 2560 BC, about 2530 years before her.
22721.m: Ancient Egypt lasted so long that Cleopatra lived closer to our time than to the building of the pyramids.

22722.q: Which number comes next in the sequence 2, 4, 8, 16, ...?
22722.e: Each number is double the one before. 16 times 2 makes 32.
22722.m: In this sequence each number is doubled.

22723.q: Which number comes next in the sequence 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ...?
22723.e: Each number is the sum of the two before it. 5 plus 8 makes 13.
22723.m: In the Fibonacci sequence you always add the last two numbers.

22724.q: Which number comes next in the sequence 3, 6, 11, 18, 27, ...?
22724.e: The gaps are 3, 5, 7 and 9, so they grow by 2 each time. The next gap is 11, and 27 plus 11 makes 38.
22724.m: With number sequences it is worth looking at the gaps between the numbers.

22725.q: A father is 36 years old and his son is 12. In how many years will the father be exactly twice as old as his son?
22725.e: In 12 years the father will be 48 and the son 24. 48 is exactly double 24.
22725.m: The age difference between two people always stays the same.

22726.q: An exercise book and a pen cost 1.10 francs together. The exercise book costs exactly 1 franc more than the pen. How much does the pen cost?
22726.e: The pen costs 5 centimes and the exercise book 1.05 francs. Together that makes 1.10 francs, and the difference is exactly 1 franc.
22726.m: With puzzles, always check your first quick answer.

22727.q: 5 machines make 5 parts in 5 minutes. How long do 100 machines take to make 100 parts?
22727.e: Each machine takes 5 minutes for one part. 100 machines work at the same time and make 100 parts in 5 minutes.
22727.m: If more machines work at the same time, the time per part stays the same.

22728.q: Water lilies double their area every day. After 30 days they cover the whole pond. After how many days did they cover half of it?
22728.e: Because the area doubles every day, the pond had been half covered one day earlier. That means day 29.
22728.m: When something doubles, half is always just one step away from the whole.

22729.q: Anna is taller than Ben. Carla is shorter than Ben. Dario is taller than Anna. Who is the shortest?
22729.e: The order from tallest to shortest is Dario, Anna, Ben, Carla. So Carla is the shortest.
22729.m: With comparison puzzles, it helps to write down the order.

22730.q: Today is Wednesday. What day of the week will it be in 10 days?
22730.e: After 7 days it is Wednesday again. 3 days later, so after 10 days, it is Saturday.
22730.m: Every seven days the same day of the week comes round again.

22731.q: Five children each shake hands with every other child once. How many handshakes are there altogether?
22731.e: Each child shakes hands with 4 others, which gives 5 times 4 equals 20. Because each handshake has been counted twice, you divide by 2 and get 10.
22731.m: With handshakes between people, you may only count each handshake once.

22732.q: A drawer has red and blue socks all mixed up. In the dark, how many socks do you need to take out at least to be sure of two of the same colour?
22732.e: With two socks you might be unlucky and get one red and one blue. But the third sock is sure to be the same colour as one of the two.
22732.m: With two colours, three socks are enough for a sure pair.

22733.q: A train leaves at 14:45 and the journey takes 1 hour and 50 minutes. When does it arrive?
22733.e: 14:45 plus 1 hour makes 15:45. Plus 50 minutes makes 16:35.
22733.m: When working out times, add the hours first and then the minutes.

22734.q: How many months of the year have at least 28 days?
22734.e: Every month has at least 28 days. February has 28 or 29 days, all the others have 30 or 31.
22734.m: Every month of the year has at least 28 days.

22735.q: In which year did Albert Einstein present the field equations of general relativity?
22735.e: Einstein presented the field equations to the Prussian Academy of Sciences in November 1915. In 1905 he had published the special theory of relativity.
22735.m: General relativity describes gravity as the curvature of spacetime.

22736.q: Who discovered in 1928 that the mould Penicillium stops bacteria from growing?
22736.e: In 1928 Fleming noticed that a mould on a bacterial culture stopped the staphylococci from growing. Penicillin was only produced in large quantities as a medicine in the 1940s.
22736.m: Penicillin was the first antibiotic to be used on a large scale.

22737.q: Who published the model of the DNA double helix in 1953?
22737.e: Watson and Crick relied, among other things, on X-ray diffraction images by Rosalind Franklin. In 1962 they received the Nobel Prize in Medicine together with Maurice Wilkins.
22737.m: DNA consists of two strands twisted around each other in a spiral.

22738.q: Which chemist arranged the elements in a periodic table in 1869 and predicted elements that were still unknown?
22738.e: Mendeleev left gaps for undiscovered elements and predicted their properties, for example for gallium and germanium. Their later discovery confirmed his system.
22738.m: With his periodic table, Mendeleev predicted elements before they were found.

22739.q: With which particle accelerator was the Higgs boson detected in 2012?
22739.e: The ATLAS and CMS experiments at CERN's Large Hadron Collider near Geneva announced the discovery in July 2012. Peter Higgs and François Englert received the Nobel Prize in Physics for it in 2013.
22739.m: The Higgs boson is linked to the mechanism that gives elementary particles their mass.

22740.q: In which year were gravitational waves measured directly for the first time?
22740.e: On 14 September 2015 the LIGO detectors in the USA recorded the signal of two merging black holes. The measurement was announced in 2016 and awarded the Nobel Prize in 2017.
22740.m: Gravitational waves are distortions of spacetime that Einstein had predicted.

22741.q: Which view of the universe did Nicolaus Copernicus set out in his main work in 1543?
a: The heliocentric view with the Sun at the centre
The geocentric view with the Earth at the centre
A view with elliptical planetary orbits
A view with the Milky Way at the centre
22741.e: In “De revolutionibus orbium coelestium”, Copernicus placed the Sun instead of the Earth at the centre of the planetary orbits. It was Johannes Kepler who later discovered that the orbits are ellipses.
22741.m: With Copernicus, the Sun moved to the centre of the picture of the universe.

22742.q: Who received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901?
22742.e: Röntgen was honoured for discovering the rays named after him (1895). Lorentz received the prize in 1902, Curie in 1903 and Planck in 1918.
22742.m: X-rays made the inside of the body visible without surgery for the first time.

22743.q: Which doctor deliberately vaccinated with cowpox for the first time in 1796 to protect against smallpox?
22743.e: Jenner transferred material from cowpox to a boy, who was then immune to smallpox. The word “vaccine” comes from the Latin “vacca” for cow.
22743.m: The word vaccine reminds us of the cowpox Jenner used.

22744.q: What assumption did Max Planck make in 1900, laying the foundation of quantum physics?
a: Energy is only given off in tiny portions
Electrons orbit on any path they like
22744.e: To explain black-body radiation, Planck assumed that energy is given off in packets of size E equals h times f. The constant h has since been called Planck's constant.
22744.m: Planck discovered that energy comes in tiny packets called quanta.

22745.q: In which year was Charles Darwin's “On the Origin of Species” published?
22745.e: Darwin published the book in 1859, explaining how species develop through natural selection. 1809 is the year he was born, 1882 the year he died.
22745.m: Darwin explained the variety of species through natural selection.

22746.q: For which development did Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna receive the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2020?
22746.e: With CRISPR/Cas9, DNA can be cut and changed at a precisely chosen point. The method was published in 2012 and spread very quickly in research.
22746.m: The CRISPR/Cas9 gene scissors can change genetic material in a targeted way.

22747.q: What height did the joint survey of Mount Everest by China and Nepal give in 2020?
22747.e: The measurement published in 2020 gave 8,848.86 m above sea level. The other values belong to K2, Kangchenjunga and Lhotse.
22747.m: At about 8,849 m, Mount Everest is the highest mountain on Earth.

22748.q: How tall is the Burj Khalifa in Dubai, the tallest building in the world (as of 2026)?
22748.e: The Burj Khalifa, opened in 2010, is 828 m tall. The Shanghai Tower is 632 m high, Merdeka 118 in Kuala Lumpur about 679 m.
22748.m: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai is the tallest building in the world.

22749.q: Which is the longest railway tunnel in the world (as of 2026)?
22749.e: The Gotthard Base Tunnel, opened in 2016, is about 57 km long. The Seikan Tunnel in Japan is about 54 km, the Channel Tunnel about 50 km.
22749.m: At about 57 km, the Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world.

22750.q: What is the men's world record for the 100 m (as of 2026)?
22750.e: Usain Bolt ran 9.58 s at the 2009 World Championships in Berlin. His Olympic winning times were 9.69 s (2008) and 9.63 s (2012).
22750.m: Usain Bolt has held the 100 m world record of 9.58 seconds since 2009.

22751.q: What is the men's marathon world record (as of 2026)?
22751.e: On 26 April 2026 the Kenyan Sabastian Sawe ran 1:59:30 h at the London Marathon, becoming the first to finish under two hours in a regular race. The old record of 2:00:35 h had been set by Kelvin Kiptum in Chicago in 2023.
22751.m: In London in 2026, Sabastian Sawe became the first to set a marathon world record under two hours.

22752.q: How many Olympic medals did the swimmer Michael Phelps win in total, a record (as of 2026)?
22752.e: Between 2004 and 2016 Phelps won 28 medals in total, 23 of them gold. The gymnast Larisa Latynina follows with 18 medals.
22752.m: Michael Phelps is the most successful Olympian of all time.

22753.q: What age did the Frenchwoman Jeanne Calment, the oldest reliably documented person, reach?
22753.e: Jeanne Calment lived from 1875 to 1997 and reached 122 years and 164 days. Her age is well supported by documents.

22754.q: Roughly how deep is the deepest known point of the oceans, in the Mariana Trench?
22754.e: Depending on the measurement, the Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench lies just under 11,000 m below sea level. Mount Everest would fit inside it.
22754.m: The deepest point of the oceans is in the Mariana Trench in the Pacific.

22755.q: Which vehicle was the first to break the sound barrier on land in 1997 and holds the speed record (as of 2026)?
22755.e: In 1997 Andy Green reached about 1,228 km/h in ThrustSSC in the Nevada desert. The vehicle was powered by two jet engines.
22755.m: In 1997 ThrustSSC became the first land vehicle to go faster than sound.

22756.q: Who holds the record for the most Grand Slam titles in men's singles (as of 2026)?
22756.e: By 2026 Novak Djokovic had won 24 Grand Slam singles titles. Rafael Nadal reached 22, Roger Federer 20.
22756.m: Novak Djokovic has won the most Grand Slam titles in men's singles.

22757.q: Which film has earned the most money worldwide, not adjusted for inflation (as of 2026)?
22757.e: James Cameron's “Avatar” (2009), including re-releases, earned about 2.9 billion US dollars. “Avengers: Endgame” follows close behind.
22757.m: Avatar is the most successful film by box office takings.

22758.q: Which ruler of a sovereign state reigned the longest on record, namely 72 years?
a: Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom
22758.e: Louis XIV became king in 1643 at the age of four and reigned until 1715. Elizabeth II reached about 70 years, Franz Joseph I about 68.
22758.m: Louis XIV reigned longer than any other known monarch of a sovereign state.

22759.q: Who is the only person to have received Nobel Prizes in two different science subjects?
22759.e: Marie Curie received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 and in Chemistry in 1911. Pauling won Chemistry and Peace, Bardeen Physics twice and Sanger Chemistry twice.
22759.m: Marie Curie received Nobel Prizes in Physics and in Chemistry.

22760.q: Which man from Geneva received the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901 together with Frédéric Passy?
22760.e: After the Battle of Solferino in 1859, Dunant had suggested founding a neutral relief organisation. This led to the Red Cross in 1863.
22760.m: Henri Dunant gave the impulse for founding the Red Cross.

22761.q: How many years in total did Nelson Mandela spend in prison before he was released in 1990?
22761.e: Mandela was imprisoned from 1962 to 1990, 18 years of it on Robben Island. In 1994 he became South Africa's first black president.
22761.m: After 27 years in prison, Nelson Mandela became president of South Africa.

22762.q: For which machine did Ada Lovelace write an algorithm in 1843 that is regarded as the first computer program?
22762.e: Lovelace described how the planned Analytical Engine could calculate Bernoulli numbers. The machine itself was never completed.
22762.m: Ada Lovelace is regarded as the first programmer in history.

22763.q: Which British mathematician played a key role in breaking the Enigma code at Bletchley Park?
22763.e: Turing developed the electromechanical “Bombe”, which was used to decode German Enigma radio messages. With the Turing machine he also created a basic model of computer science.
22763.m: Alan Turing is regarded as one of the fathers of computer science.

22764.q: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi lead the Salt March against the British salt monopoly?
22764.e: In 1930 Gandhi marched about 385 km to the sea to make salt there, which was forbidden. The non-violent protest made the Indian independence movement known around the world.
22764.m: Gandhi fought for India's independence with non-violent resistance.

22765.q: In which Swiss city did Albert Einstein work at the patent office when he published his groundbreaking papers in 1905?
22765.e: From 1902 Einstein was a technical expert at the Federal Office for Intellectual Property in Bern. 1905 is known as his “miracle year”.
22765.m: Einstein wrote his famous papers of 1905 while working at the patent office in Bern.

22766.q: Who is the highest summit in Switzerland named after?
22766.e: The 4,634 m Dufourspitze in the Monte Rosa massif honours General Dufour. He also directed the first accurate national map of Switzerland, the Dufour Map.
22766.m: The Dufourspitze bears the name of the general and cartographer Dufour.

22767.q: At which event did Martin Luther King give his “I Have a Dream” speech in 1963?
a: The march from Selma to Montgomery
22767.e: In front of more than 200,000 people at the Lincoln Memorial, King spoke for civil rights and against racial segregation. He received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964.
22767.m: Martin Luther King fought non-violently for equal rights for black people in the USA.

22768.q: Which Kenyan environmental activist became the first African woman to receive the Nobel Peace Prize in 2004?
22768.e: Maathai founded the Green Belt Movement, which planted millions of trees. Johnson Sirleaf, Gbowee and Karman were only honoured in 2011.
22768.m: Wangari Maathai linked environmental protection with peace and democracy.

22769.q: Who became the first woman President of the Swiss Confederation in 1999?
22769.e: Ruth Dreifuss was a Federal Councillor from 1993 to 2002 and President of the Confederation in 1999. Elisabeth Kopp became the first woman Federal Councillor in 1984 but was never President.
22769.m: Ruth Dreifuss was the first woman at the head of the Federal Council.

22770.q: How many member states does the United Nations have (as of 2026)?
22770.e: Since South Sudan joined in 2011, the UN has had 193 members. The Holy See and Palestine have observer status.

22771.q: Which country is NOT a permanent member of the UN Security Council with a veto?
22771.e: The permanent members are the USA, Russia, China, France and the United Kingdom. Germany has several times been a non-permanent member for two years.
22771.m: The UN Security Council has five permanent members with a veto.

22772.q: In which year did Switzerland join the United Nations as a full member?
22772.e: The people voted in favour of joining in March 2002, after clearly rejecting it in 1986. Switzerland became the 190th member in September 2002.
22772.m: Switzerland has only been a member of the UN since 2002.

22773.q: How many times has the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) received the Nobel Peace Prize (as of 2026)?
22773.e: The ICRC was honoured in 1917, 1944 and 1963, in 1963 together with the League of Red Cross Societies. Its headquarters are in Geneva.
22773.m: The ICRC in Geneva is one of the most honoured organisations in the world.

22774.q: Which organisation replaced the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) in 1995?
22774.e: The WTO, based in Geneva, sets the rules for world trade and settles trade disputes. It grew out of the GATT of 1947 in 1995.
22774.m: The WTO in Geneva sets rules for world trade.

22775.q: In which year was the World Health Organization (WHO) founded?
22775.e: The WHO constitution came into force on 7 April 1948, which is why this day is World Health Day. The WHO is a specialised agency of the UN based in Geneva.
22775.m: The WHO was founded in 1948 as the UN's health organisation.

22776.q: Which treaty founded the European Union in 1992?
22776.e: The treaty, signed in 1992, came into force in 1993 and also set the path to a common currency. The Treaties of Rome of 1957 had created the EEC.
22776.m: The European Union was created by the Treaty of Maastricht.

22777.q: When was NATO's Article 5 mutual defence clause invoked for the first time?
a: At the start of the Korean War in 1950
During the Cuban Missile Crisis in 1962
22777.e: Article 5 states that an attack on one member counts as an attack on all. It has only been used once so far, after the terrorist attacks in the USA.
22777.m: Under Article 5, an attack on one NATO member counts as an attack on all.

22778.q: At which conference were the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank agreed in 1944?
22778.e: At Bretton Woods (USA), 44 countries agreed a new monetary order with fixed exchange rates. The system of fixed rates ended in the early 1970s.
22778.m: The IMF and World Bank were agreed at Bretton Woods in 1944.

22779.q: Which international financial organisation has its headquarters in Basel?
22779.e: The BIS was founded in 1930 and is known as the “central banks' bank”. The ECB is in Frankfurt, the IMF in Washington, the EIB in Luxembourg.
22779.m: The central banks' bank has its headquarters in Basel.

22780.q: Which country belongs to EFTA alongside Switzerland, Norway and Iceland (as of 2026)?
22780.e: Austria, Denmark and the United Kingdom used to be EFTA members but joined the EU. Today EFTA has only four members.
22780.m: EFTA today consists of Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Iceland.

22781.q: To which organisation, of which Switzerland has been a member since 1963, does the European Court of Human Rights belong?
22781.e: The Council of Europe in Strasbourg is not part of the EU and has 46 member states (as of 2026). It watches over the European Convention on Human Rights.
22781.m: The Council of Europe protects human rights and is independent of the EU.

22782.q: Which peace settlement of 1648 recognised under international law that the Swiss Confederacy was separate from the Holy Roman Empire?
22782.e: The mayor of Basel, Johann Rudolf Wettstein, achieved this recognition in the peace negotiations at the end of the Thirty Years' War. In 1499 the Confederacy had only broken away in practice.
22782.m: Since 1648 the independence of the Swiss Confederacy has been recognised under international law.

22783.q: At which gathering did the great powers recognise Switzerland's permanent neutrality in 1815?
22783.e: The Congress of Vienna reorganised Europe after Napoleon and largely fixed Switzerland's borders. Neutrality was formally confirmed in Paris in November 1815.
22783.m: Switzerland's neutrality has been internationally recognised since 1815.

22784.q: What helped the Industrial Revolution to begin in Great Britain in the 18th century?
a: Rich coal and iron deposits and plenty of capital from trade
A ban on all overseas trade
22784.e: Coal supplied energy for steam engines, iron the material for machines. Profits from trade and colonies made it possible to invest in factories.
22784.m: Coal, iron and capital made Great Britain the pioneer of industrialisation.
